VERIFIED BY EYE before committing: an unimproved earth two-track running from the camera's feet, curving, over a rise and on to the horizon, through low sagebrush and bunchgrass under a partly clouded blue sky, rolling ground, no built structure in frame. EXIF: Apple iPhone XR, 2021-06-26 09:07:31, 26 mm 35 mm-equivalent, f/1.8, 1/1916 s, ISO 25, orientation 1 (upright). No GPS in the file, so the location is not established and is not asserted here.
note:
THE FAR-BAND ROAD REFERENCE, for R-M1b, and the complement to samstone_2017_tallgrass_trail rather than its replacement. Each anchors what it is actually good for.

WHY THIS ONE CARRIES THE FAR BANDS. The track is unbroken from the foreground to the horizon at 4032x3024, so a contrast can be read at every distance the gate scores - which the Kansas photograph cannot do past about twenty metres at 593x400. It is also a DIRECT DIGITAL CAPTURE, not a scan of a print, so its sRGB values are not mediated by film stock and scanner and absolute readings are defensible here in a way they are not there.

THE FRAME IS ALREADY SOLVED, by the same arithmetic as the sky reference and by coincidence of the same lens. 26 mm equivalent over 3024 px gives 53.1 deg vertical and 57.0 px/deg, so once the horizon row is found the elevation of any pixel is (horizon - row) / 57.0 degrees. saari_2018_dupage_tallgrass was shot at the same 26 mm equivalent, so the two references share a frame model.

AND THE DATE IS FIVE DAYS OFF THE SCENE. 26 June against a scene date of 1 July - closer than any other reference this project holds, and it removes the season caveat that the September Kansas photograph carries.

THE BIAS THAT MUST NOT BE FORGOTTEN WHEN DERIVING FROM IT. This is SAGEBRUSH STEPPE, not tallgrass prairie: pale silver Artemisia and short bunchgrass on dry rolling ground. Pale dust against pale sage is a LOW-contrast pairing; dark earth against deep-green July tallgrass on the Chicago lake plain is a higher-contrast one. A threshold derived here therefore comes out LOWER than Chicago's true one, and a gate set from it would pass roads in the reconstruction that are genuinely too faint to see - which is the exact failure this whole bug is made of. Derive the far-band SHAPE from this file (how contrast falls with distance) and take the near-field MAGNITUDE from the tallgrass photograph, or state plainly that the bar is conservative and why.
what_it_supplies: the fall of earth-track contrast with distance, from underfoot to the horizon, at a resolution that resolves the track in every band the road gate scores
a direct digital capture whose absolute sRGB is not mediated by film, print or scanner, unlike the Kansas scan
a frame model: 26 mm equivalent over 3024 px = 57.0 px/deg, the same lens geometry as the sky reference, so elevation per pixel is computable once the horizon row is found
a date five days from the scene date, 26 June against 1 July
what_it_does_not_supply: tallgrass prairie - it is sagebrush steppe, pale Artemisia and bunchgrass on dry ground; the earth-against-vegetation contrast here is LOWER than deep-green July tallgrass would give, so any threshold derived from it is conservative and must be labelled so
the flat lake plain - the ground is rolling, so a horizon here is a ridge line rather than the true horizon Chicago's sightlines have
a location - the file carries no GPS and none is asserted
wagon-road width - this is a single-vehicle two-track; an 1835 street was a platted corridor about ten metres wide, and only the surface contrast transfers
